projects.title: qrate
projects.organization: Personal project · COMP 440 Directed Studies, University of the Fraser Valley
projects.description: An open-source desktop cataloguing app for archives, libraries and museums. It keeps the spreadsheet grid archivists already know, validates metadata against real standards as it is typed, and shows each record's scans, documents and video beside it. In beta with the South Asian Canadian Digital Archive and other institutions, iterating on live feedback from archivists.
details: Used by the South Asian Studies Institute's research assistants to catalogue SACDA collections; their requests (bulk editing first) set the roadmap
330+ release downloads; signed builds for macOS, Windows and Linux shipped through the Microsoft Store, a Homebrew tap and background in-app updates
Validates as you type: LCSH, Wikidata and GeoNames authority checks, EDTF dates, missing linked files and Hunspell spelling, shown as squiggles and in a Problems panel with one-click fixes
15-crate Rust workspace on GPUI (the GPU UI framework behind the Zed editor), with a virtualised grid and cached thumbnail gallery that stay smooth on ~2,000-row scan-backed collections
Projects are portable single-file SQLite databases; import CSV, Excel, OpenDocument, a folder tree or a Google Sheet, export CSV, Excel, JSON-LD, CSL-JSON or ZIP, with two-way Google Sheets sync
Optional local visual search ranks images, PDF pages and video frames against a text description, with the model running on the archivist's machine
Sandboxed Luau plugin system with permissions and a signed plugin registry; the Islandora plugin checks columns against a live repository's vocabularies
Read-only AI agent bridge: an agent (bundled or external) can stage findings in the Problems panel but never writes a cell
PDFium and ffmpeg are loaded at runtime instead of linked, so the app ships at 73 MB while previewing PDFs, multi-page TIFFs, audio and video
Started as an AI metadata assistant at Hack the North 2025; AGPL-3.0 with contributions from 4 other developers

projects.title: Islandora contributions
projects.description: Open-source contributor to Islandora, the Drupal-based digital repository platform used by libraries and archives, focused on ecosystem tooling, high-throughput migration and ingestion, and digital preservation workflows. Most of it comes out of moving SACDA onto Islandora.
details: isle-buildkit: traced animated GIFs producing no derivatives to ImageMagick writing one file per frame in the Houdini image service, and fixed it by reading only the first frame (issue #609, PR #610)
islandora_dxpr: print stylesheet so researchers can print an item or collection record for citation, with the title, image, full metadata and citation but no navigation or viewer chrome (PR #44)
Replacing legacy Java media-processing microservices with a Go + libvips pipeline that generates pyramidal TIFFs, to cut server resource use and processing latency while improving image quality
Working with Fedora and OCFL (Oxford Common File Layout) for standards-compliant preservation storage and derivative generation
qrate's Islandora plugin brings a live Islandora site's controlled vocabularies into cataloguing

projects.title: Clash of Code (LAN edition)
projects.description: A multiplayer competitive-programming game inspired by CodinGame's Clash of Code that runs on a local network, so a whole class can race to solve the same problem. My 10th grade final project for my programming course, built with Python and PyQt5.
details: Client/server over the LAN: a PyQt5 client with login, problem and results screens, and a server GUI to host a round

Round settings for mode (e.g. shortest code), time limit, task description and examples, plus ready-made problem presets
Account database managed from the command line, and a setup script that creates desktop shortcuts for the client and server

projects.title: Mac media server
projects.description: Scripts from my native Jellyfin setup on an Apple Silicon Mac with media on an external SSD: Live TV for India and Canada with a daily XMLTV guide, anime library configuration, subtitles, SMB sharing and monitoring.
details: Live TV: filters iptv-org playlists to the channels I want, probes every stream with Jellyfin's ffprobe and registers the tuners through the Jellyfin API
Maps playlist channels to guide sources and rebuilds a two-day XMLTV guide daily, publishing atomically and keeping the last good guide if a grab fails
Guide checkout lives on an APFS sparse image because its many small files were slow on the exFAT media drive; Beszel for monitoring, Tailscale for remote access
